title: Genuine VRRP VIP migration between the HAProxy HA pair
description: Drives a real keepalived VRRP failover by stopping nexus-haproxy.service on the current MASTER (haproxy-pg-1, priority 110). The check_haproxy.sh script detects the failure within fall=3 × interval=2 = ~6 s; weight=-30 demotes haproxy-pg-1's effective priority from 110 to 80, below haproxy-pg-2's 100. haproxy-pg-2 transitions BACKUP -> MASTER + binds VIP .60. App connections to <VIP>:5432 see a brief blip and then resume. Mirrors the operational pattern from 0.G.3 demo-12 (redis failover) but at the LB tier.

prerequisites.smokeGate: smoke-0.G.4.ps1 ALL GREEN (VIP bound on exactly 1 haproxy node + cert IP-SAN includes VIP)

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.67 'ip -4 addr show dev nic0 | grep 192.168.70.60'

observe.what: VIP 192.168.70.60 currently bound on haproxy-pg-1 (MASTER) as a /24 secondary on nic0

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.68 'ip -4 addr show dev nic0 | grep 192.168.70.60 || echo NO_VIP_ON_BACKUP'

observe.what: haproxy-pg-2 (BACKUP) does NOT hold the VIP -- exactly-one-MASTER invariant holds
Within ~6 s: 'Backup received priority 0 advertisement from <self>' then 'Entering FAULT STATE' as check_haproxy.sh fails (weight=-30 fires)

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.68 'ip -4 addr show dev nic0 | grep 192.168.70.60'

observe.what: VIP 192.168.70.60 now bound on haproxy-pg-2 -- migration complete
'Entering MASTER STATE' + 'setting promote_secondaries on interface nic0' + VIP added

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.61 'SUPER_PWD=$(sudo cat /etc/nexus-patroni/postgres-superuser-password); PGPASSWORD="$SUPER_PWD" psql "host=192.168.70.60 port=5432 user=nexusops dbname=postgres sslmode=verify-full sslrootcert=/etc/ssl/certs/patroni-ca.pem" -tA -c "SELECT now();"'

observe.what: psql via VIP works post-failover; haproxy-pg-2 now serves :5432; TLS handshake validates against verify-full (the cert IP-SAN covers the VIP)
haproxy-pg-2's nexus-haproxy log shows a new client connection accepted on :5432, forwarded to the current Patroni leader's backend
Within ~6 s: 'check_haproxy.sh' succeeds again (rise=2); 'Received advert with higher priority' from peer; entering MASTER state

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@192.168.70.67 ip -4 addr show dev nic0 | grep 192.168.70.60
observe.what: VIP back on haproxy-pg-1 (preempt ON; lab visible-demo default. Set nopreempt to avoid flap in production)

whatProves: keepalived unicast VRRP elects exactly one MASTER across the haproxy HA pair (no split-brain because unicast bypasses VMware VMnet11's unreliable multicast forwarding). On MASTER health-script failure, BACKUP promotes itself within fall × interval = ~6 s; the VIP migrates at the kernel L3 layer; apps connecting to <VIP>:5432 see continuous service across a single-node HAProxy failure. The cert IP-SAN design means client sslmode=verify-full works against the floating VIP regardless of which haproxy currently holds it. The HA pair eliminates the SPOF that a single HAProxy would have had; the 'HA' promise in the phase name now covers the entire path.
